question: In a certain code language, ‘CLUTCH’ is written as ‘DNXXHN’ and ‘CREDIT’ is written as ‘DTHHNZ’. How will ‘WALLET’ be written in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is:

For, 'CLUTCH’ is written as ‘DNXXHN',

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec27755753fc22e8634ead3b197ac79f2a00a80df1ccb524a4d8d804ccdec6b4.png] 

For, 'CREDIT’ is written as ‘DTHHNZ',

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df348bbb1c456cbbadab519e2ddfe8c037ce1fecfeefc1d15991b79621aa4e83.png] 

Similarly, for '**WALLET**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cacf4b4e4abbc9be4ad576652dcbecd52cbf7b8dbc2258f7919dc1010e8791b9.png] 

So, '**WALLET**' will be written as '**XCOPJZ**'.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
